intro: Look out from the terraces of Arykanda Ancient City, in Antalya province. This spectacular Lycian city, built on terraces facing the mountains, spans the 5th century BC to the 6th century AD, and it offers a unique panorama over the Finike plain.
history: Arykanda was a member of the Lycian League, inhabited from the 5th century BC, and its terraced urban layout took shape during the Hellenistic and Roman periods. In the 2nd century AD came a major building boom. Then, in the 6th century, earthquakes struck: the city was severely damaged and was gradually abandoned.
structure-3: You are now at the Odeon and Bouleuterion, two halls standing side by side. Here people gathered for assemblies and for performances. Imagine the voices of both filling this corner of the city.
highlights: As you wander up the terraces, don't miss the Theatre and the Stadium, the Agora and the Roman Baths.
facts: Did you know? Arykanda is one of the rare ancient cities built on five large rock-cut terraces ascending a mountainside. Theatre, stadium and baths are stacked one above another up the steep slope, and its view is singled out among ancient cities. Even its name tells a story: the '-anda' ending is native Anatolian, showing the city existed long before Greek colonisation. And a final detail: ancient sources remark on the Arykandans' appetite for pleasure, and on their debts.
outro: This brings our climb through Arykanda Ancient City to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Take one last look at the view before you go. Enjoy your visit.
